title: How Long Does Carpet Last? When to Replace Carpet in Kirkland Homes
meta: Carpet lasts 5 to 15 years depending on fiber, pad and traffic. Wills Flooring explains the signs it is time to replace carpet in Kirkland homes, or wait.
keywords: how long does carpet last, when to replace carpet, carpet lifespan by fiber, signs carpet needs replacing, replace carpet Kirkland WA, carpet padding worn out

blocks.lead: Most carpet lasts 5 to 15 years: builder-grade polyester 5 to 7, mid-grade nylon 10 to 12, quality nylon or triexta on a good pad 15 or more, and wool 20 plus. Replace it when the pile stops recovering, the pad has broken down, or odors survive a professional cleaning.
blocks.detail: Fiber sets the ceiling, but pad, vacuuming and traffic decide whether you reach it. Most of the carpet we replace in Kirkland is not worn through; it is matted, tired and sitting on a pad that turned to crumbs years ago. Replacing it is $0.99 per sq ft in labor, $0.45 to pull the old carpet and pad out, plus the carpet and pad you choose.

blocks.html: Kirkland has a lot of carpet at the end of its second life. Homes in Juanita, Rose Hill and Totem Lake built between the 1970s and 1990s were carpeted at construction, recarpeted once around 2005, and are now being weighed by owners who either want to stay another decade or want to sell to buyers with high expectations. Both groups ask the same thing: is it done, or can it go another few years?

items.title: The pad dies first
items.text: Rebond padding loses its bounce years before the carpet fibers wear out. Once it goes flat, every step grinds the carpet backing against the subfloor, and the carpet ripples because it is no longer supported. Push your heel down hard; if it feels like standing on plywood, the pad is done.

items.title: Traffic lanes and crushing
items.text: The path from the garage door to the kitchen takes thousands of steps a week and the guest room takes a few dozen. Crushed pile in the lane reflects light differently, so it looks dirty even when it is clean. Nylon springs back; polyester and olefin do not.

items.title: Grit, not dirt
items.text: Fine sand tracked in from the Cross Kirkland Corridor trail or a gravel driveway sits at the base of the pile and cuts fibers every time you walk. Weekly vacuuming roughly doubles carpet life because it removes grit before it does damage.

items.title: Sun, stains and pets
items.text: West-facing windows over Lake Washington fade carpet in a few summers. Pet accidents that reach the pad come back as odor every humid week. Neither wears the carpet out mechanically, but both end its life just as surely.

blocks.text: Seven signs it is time to replace

items.html: Matting that a cleaning does not fix. If the traffic lane still looks flat and dark after a professional hot-water extraction, the fibers have lost their twist. Nothing brings it back.
The pad has broken down. Crumbs at the edge when you lift a corner, or a floor that feels hard underfoot, means the carpet is now wearing against the subfloor.
Odor that returns. Smells that come back a week after cleaning live in the pad or the subfloor, not the carpet. New carpet on the old pad will smell the same.
Allergies that improve when you travel. Old carpet holds a decade of dust, dander and pollen deep in the pile. If symptoms ease in a hotel, the carpet is a suspect.
Stains that wick back. A stain that reappears after cleaning has soaked the backing. Patching works for one spot, not for a room full.
Seams opening and edges fraying. Once the backing delaminates, seams split under foot traffic and the carpet cannot be re-stretched without tearing.
Ripples, but only if the pad is also gone. Ripples alone can be re-stretched in an afternoon. Ripples on a dead pad mean the carpet is at the end.

blocks.title: Selling in Kirkland:
blocks.text: Buyers in Houghton, Bridle Trails and along the Juanita waterfront discount tired carpet by more than it costs to replace, and fresh neutral carpet photographs well. Before you recarpet, lift a corner in a closet. Many 1970s and 1980s Kirkland homes have oak under the carpet, and a refinish at $3.99 per sq ft can be the better upgrade.
How to make the next carpet last 15 years

items.html: Buy the pad, not just the carpet. An 8 lb density rebond or a frothed polyurethane pad supports the carpet and is the single biggest factor in how long it lasts.
Choose a resilient fiber. Solution-dyed nylon or triexta in a dense cut pile. Save polyester for a guest room.
Vacuum weekly with the head set correctly. A beater bar set too low shreds pile; set too high it removes nothing. Adjust until the vacuum pulls slightly.
Professional cleaning every 12 to 18 months. Most manufacturer warranties require it, and it removes the grit that cuts fibers.
Mats at every entry and shoes off. The cheapest life extension there is. Our carpet installation page covers what else is included when you are ready.

faq.q: Does a 20-year carpet warranty mean the carpet lasts 20 years?
faq.a: No. Most long warranties cover wear-through to the backing, which almost never happens, and exclude matting, crushing, stains and traffic lanes, which is how carpet actually ages. Treat a warranty as a statement about fiber quality, not a lifespan. Read what is excluded before you compare two carpets by warranty length.

faq.q: How often should carpet be replaced in a rental?
faq.a: Every 7 to 10 years for a mid-grade nylon in a typical Kirkland rental, sooner if tenants have pets. Landlords who install dense nylon over a good pad usually get two or three tenancies out of it; builder-grade polyester often needs replacing between tenants after five years.

Wool and top-grade nylon over a dense pad can, in a household that vacuums weekly, keeps shoes off and has it professionally cleaned. Most carpet that old is replaced for style rather than wear. Realistically, plan on 12 to 15 years for a good carpet and treat anything beyond that as a bonus.

faq.q: Does professional cleaning extend carpet life?
faq.a: Yes, meaningfully. Hot-water extraction removes the grit at the base of the pile that cuts fibers with every step, and it lifts crushed pile in traffic lanes if the fiber still has twist. Cleaning every 12 to 18 months is also a condition of most manufacturer warranties.

faq.q: How can I tell if the carpet pad is worn out?
faq.a: Press your heel down hard in a traffic lane. Good pad compresses and springs back; dead pad feels like the subfloor with a rug on it. Lift a corner near a closet: crumbling foam or a pad that has flattened to half its thickness means it is finished, even if the carpet on top looks acceptable.

faq.q: Should I replace carpet before selling my Kirkland house?
faq.a: Usually yes if the carpet is stained, matted or dated, because Kirkland buyers discount it heavily and new neutral carpet photographs well. Labor is $0.99 per sq ft plus $0.45 to tear the old carpet out, so it is a cheap listing fix. Check under a corner first: if there is hardwood beneath, refinishing may return more.
